mainTopic: Closures that may look like building on שבת and יום טוב, and unlocking doors across domains (רבי מאיר and the חכמים)
overview: The amud opens with a משנה: makeshift closures like a back-court door, thorn bundles in a breach, or mats may close an opening on שבת only if they are raised off the ground, so that closing them does not look like בנין. A ברייתא seems to require only that they be tied and hanging. אביי explains that it means closures with a ציר (hinge), and רבא says it is enough if they once had one. A second ברייתא requires raising, and each אמורא reads it as 'hinge OR raised'. The גמרא adds rulings on thorn bundles and on a 'widowed door', and רב יהודה's rule that a woodpile and similar items on יום טוב must be set up top-down, not bottom-up. A story follows in which רבי יהושע בן חנניה turns a heretic's insult about 'thorns' into praise of the righteous. A new משנה then has רבי מאיר forbid unlocking a door across רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים without a ten-טפחים partition, and the חכמים answer with a story from a market in ירושלים. The גמרא asks how a story about a כרמלית can answer a ruling about רשות הרבים. רב פפא answers that the story happened after the walls were breached. רבא begins rereading the end of the משנה as a case of garden gates, and that rereading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: makeshift closures must be raised off the ground
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a back-court door, thorn bundles in a breach, and mats may not be used to close an opening on שבת unless they are raised above the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A door of a back courtyard, bundles of thorns used to fill a breach, and mats: one may not close an opening with them on שבת unless they are raised above the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three makeshift closures and says you may close an opening with them on שבת only if they hang above the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are not real doors. Putting one into an opening can look like building a wall, which is a form of בנין. If the item stays raised off the ground, it looks more like a door being swung shut and less like building.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a back courtyard behind the house (not the usual meaning of מוקצה)
A breach or gap in a wall

steps.confusionAlert: The word מוקצה here does NOT mean items forbidden to move on שבת. It means a back courtyard behind the house.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule, 'raised off the ground'. The whole סוגיא tests it against ברייתות.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The door that is in the rear courtyard,
and bundles of thorns that are in a breach, and mats —
phrases.notes: All three are makeshift, not real doors.

phrases.english: one may not close an opening with them
phrases.notes: Doing so could look like building.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גְּבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: unless they are raised above the ground.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Makeshift closures may be used on שבת only if they are raised off the ground.

steps.title: A ברייתא that only requires tying and hanging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. A ברייתא permits dragging doors, mats and lattices if they are tied and hanging, and it says nothing about being raised.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And they contrasted it with a ברייתא: A dragging door, a dragging mat, and a dragging lattice, when they are tied and hanging, one may close an opening with them on שבת, and it goes without saying on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the משנה against a ברייתא that seems to give an easier rule. The ברייתא only requires the items to be tied and hanging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes items that drag along the ground, so they are not raised. Even so, it allows them once they are tied and hanging. The משנה demands that the items be raised off the ground, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it' – introduces a contradiction between two sources
A lattice or woven screen used as a closure

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they contrasted it:
a door that drags and a mat that drags,
and a lattice that drags,
when they are tied and hanging —
phrases.notes: No mention of being raised off the ground.

phrases.english: one may close an opening with them on שבת,
and needless to say on יום טוב!
phrases.notes: יום טוב is more lenient than שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the משנה's requirement of being raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that closures be raised off the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows dragging items that are merely tied and hanging, so being raised seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא is about doors with a hinge
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is talking about closures that have a ציר (hinge). That is why they do not need to be raised.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא is talking about a case where they have a hinge.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A closure with a hinge works like a real door, so closing it does not look like building, even if it drags. The משנה is talking about makeshift closures without hinges, and those must be raised.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a case where they have a hinge,
phrases.notes: A hinge gives it the status of a real door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה describe the same kind of closure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about hinged closures, which need no raising. The משנה is about unhinged ones, which must be raised.

steps.title: רבא: even if it once had a hinge
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a more lenient answer. The ברייתא applies even to closures that once had a hinge, even if they no longer have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even a case where they once had a hinge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, broader way to resolve the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a closure that used to hang on a hinge still looks like a door. So closing it does not look like building. Only closures that never had a hinge fall under the משנה's requirement to be raised.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the small difference: יש (has now) for אביי versus היה (had in the past) for רבא. That one word is the whole מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a case where they once had a hinge.
phrases.notes: Past tense makes it broader than אביי's answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the same contradiction, broader than אביי's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a closure that has a hinge right now counts as a door.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a closure that once had a hinge keeps the look of a door and needs no raising.

steps.title: A second ברייתא requires raising even a hair's breadth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about the same dragging items. It requires them to be tied, hanging, AND raised even a hair's breadth, which seems to challenge the answers just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: A dragging door, a dragging mat, and a dragging lattice, when they are tied and hanging and raised from the ground even a hair's breadth, one may close an opening with them. And if not, one may not close an opening with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection from a second ברייתא. That ברייתא does require being raised for these same dragging items. The next step answers this objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא seemed to say that tying and hanging is enough, and אביי and רבא explained that the items have (or had) a hinge. Now a ברייתא about the identical list of items adds a requirement to be raised. This suggests that being raised is needed even for these items, so the explanation needs to be defended.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They objected' – introduces a challenge from a ברייתא
The width of a single hair

phrases.english: They objected:
a door that drags, and a mat that drags,
and a lattice that drags,
when they are tied and hanging

phrases.aramaic: וּגְבוֹהִים מִן הָאָרֶץ אֲפִילּוּ מְלֹא נִימָא —
phrases.english: and raised from the ground even a hair's breadth —
phrases.notes: The new requirement that was missing in the first ברייתא.

phrases.english: one may close an opening with them,
and if not — one may not close an opening with them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answers of אביי and רבא with a parallel ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answers of אביי and רבא that the dragging items in the ברייתא need no raising.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the very same dragging items explicitly requires them to be raised, even minimally. So tying and hanging (with a hinge) seems not to be enough.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three sources: the משנה (must be raised), ברייתא 1 (tied and hanging is enough), and ברייתא 2 (tied, hanging, and raised a hair's breadth). אביי and רבא used a hinge to explain ברייתא 1, and now ברייתא 2 pressures that explanation.

steps.title: אביי and רבא each fit the second baraita into their own view
steps.stepSummary: Both אביי and רבא answer the challenge by reading the second ברייתא as offering two alternatives: a hinge (according to each one's view of what counts) OR being raised off the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי answers according to his own view, and רבא answers according to his own view. אביי reads it: either they have a hinge, or they are raised off the ground. רבא reads it: either they once had a hinge, or they are raised off the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. Each אמורא shows that the 'raised' requirement in the second ברייתא is just one of two options, not a requirement for every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא seemed to require that every closure be raised. Both אמוראים read it as 'hinge OR raised.' If there is a hinge, no raising is needed. Without a hinge, raising is needed. אביי requires a hinge that is there now. רבא is satisfied with a hinge that was there once.
steps.whatToRemember: A closure that drags may be used on שבת if it is tied and hanging AND either has a hinge or is raised off the ground. For אביי the hinge must be there now. For רבא it is enough that it once had a hinge.
steps.confusionAlert: The two ברייתות do not argue with each other. The second ברייתא simply spells out the 'raised' option, which applies to closures that have no hinge.

phrases.english: Abaye reconciles it according to his reasoning,
and Rava reconciles it according to his reasoning.
Abaye reconciles it according to his reasoning:
either they have a hinge,
phrases.notes: A hinge that is there now

phrases.english: or they are raised off the ground.
Rava reconciles it according to his reasoning:
when they once had a hinge,
phrases.notes: Past tense: even if the hinge is gone now

phrases.english: or they are raised off the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא as listing two alternative conditions (hinge OR raised)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second ברייתא requires every dragging closure to be raised, which would contradict the hinge answers
steps.terutzMaskana: Raising is needed only when there is no hinge. Each אמורא keeps his own definition of what counts as a hinge.

steps.title: Tied and hanging thorn bundles may be used to close a breach
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that thorn branches and bundles set up to close a breach in a courtyard may be used to close it on שבת when they are tied and hanging, and certainly on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: thorn branches and bundles that were prepared to close a breach in a courtyard, when they are tied and hanging, may be used to close it on שבת, and needless to say on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about the thorn bundles mentioned in the משנה. It explains when they may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied and hanging shows that the bundles serve as a fixed doorway, so closing with them is like closing a door, not building a wall. 'Needless to say on יום טוב' teaches that יום טוב is more lenient here than שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a breach / gap in a wall

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Thorn branches and bundles
that one prepared for a breach in a courtyard,
when they are tied and hanging —
one may close with them on Shabbat,
and needless to say on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a further source on the thorn bundles from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tied and hanging thorn bundles that close a courtyard breach may be used to close it on שבת, and all the more so on יום טוב

steps.title: רבי חייא: a dragging 'widowed door' may not be used
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that a 'widowed door' that drags along the ground may not be used to close an opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: a 'widowed door' that drags — one may not close with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי חייא that forbids closing with a certain kind of door. The unusual name 'widowed door' sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because this door drags and does not look like a real door, closing it looks like building rather than shutting a door. The term needs a definition, which the גמרא asks for next.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'widowed door', a door missing something that makes it a normal door

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
A 'widowed door' that drags —
one may not close with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling about closures, this time a forbidden one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dragging 'widowed door' may not be used to close an opening on שבת

steps.title: What is a 'widowed door'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly is meant by a 'widowed door'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a 'widowed door'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term from רבי חייא's teaching. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for information, not an attack. The ruling only makes sense once we know what makes a door 'widowed'.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how do we picture it?

phrases.english: What is the case of a 'widowed door'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term used in Step 8

steps.title: Two definitions of a widowed door
steps.stepSummary: One view says it is a door made of a single plank. Another view says it is a door with no threshold beneath it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is a door made of one plank, and some say it is a door that has no threshold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two explanations of what makes a door 'widowed'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first view, a single plank does not look like a real door. Under the second view, a door with no threshold touches the ground, so it drags. Either way the door is missing a normal feature, so closing it looks like building.

phrases.english: Some say: one made of a single plank,
and some say: one that has no threshold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a single-plank door, or a door with no threshold that touches the ground

steps.title: רב יהודה: stacking wood for a fire top-down is permitted, bottom-up is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that arranging wood for a fire on יום טוב from the top down is permitted, but from the bottom up is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: with a fire pile, from the top down it is permitted; from the bottom up it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on a related idea: avoiding actions that look like building. It is about setting up a wood pile for a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building normally goes from the bottom up, so stacking wood that way looks like building. If you hold the upper wood in the air and slip the lower pieces underneath (top down), it does not follow the building pattern, so it is allowed. This matches the closure rules above, where the issue was also whether something looks like building.

keyTerms.meaning: a pile of wood for a fire

steps.confusionAlert: 'Top down' does not mean placing the top piece first on the ground. It means the upper wood is held up while the lower wood is put in beneath it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle: an action is treated as building when it follows the normal order of building, from the ground up.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This fire pile,
from the top down — permitted,
from the bottom up — forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related topic: actions forbidden because they look like building
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arranging firewood from the top down is permitted. Arranging it from the bottom up is forbidden because it resembles building.

steps.title: The same rule applies to eggs, a pot, a bed, and barrels
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's top-down rule also applies to arranging eggs, setting a pot on supports, setting up a bed, and stacking barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same applies to eggs, and the same to a pot, and the same to a bed, and the same to barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב יהודה's statement. It lists more cases where you must hold the top item up first and slide the bottom pieces underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building from the bottom up looks like making a 'tent' (אהל), so it is forbidden on יום טוב. Holding the top item in the air and then putting the supports under it is not normal building. That method is allowed for every item on this list.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, anything stacked into a tent-like shape must be put together top-first: hold the top up, then slide the base under it.

phrases.english: And the same with eggs, and the same with a pot,
phrases.notes: Eggs stacked in a pile; a pot placed on stones over the fire.

phrases.english: and the same with a bed, and the same with barrels.
phrases.notes: A bed set on its frame; barrels stacked in a cellar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב יהודה's top-down rule to more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs, pots, beds, and barrels must be arranged top-first on יום טוב.

steps.title: A heretic mocks רבי יהושע בן חנניה as a 'man of thorns'
steps.stepSummary: A heretic insults the Jews by quoting a verse that says even their best are like thorns.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: 'Thorn-man! For it is written about you: "The best of them is like a thorn."'
steps.whatsHappening: Since thorn bundles came up earlier, the גמרא tells a related story. A heretic uses a verse from מיכה to mock the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic reads the verse literally: even Israel's 'best' are only thorns, meaning worthless and harmful. This is an attack on the honor of the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The best of them is like a thorn' (מיכה ז:ד)

phrases.english: A certain heretic said to him
to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:
Thorn-man!
For it is written about you: "The best of them is like a thorn."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An aggadic side story linked by the theme of thorns from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The honor of the Jewish people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A literal reading of the verse calls Israel's best people 'thorns'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers: read the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע calls the heretic a fool and points to the end of the verse, which shows the verse is not simply an insult.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Fool! Go down to the end of the verse, where it is written: "The upright one is from a thorn hedge."'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back. He tells the heretic to read the whole verse and not just the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the verse calls the person 'ישר', upright, so the verse cannot simply be calling Israel worthless. Reading part of a verse out of context gives a false meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Go down to the end of the verse

phrases.english: He said to him: Fool!
Go down to the end of the verse,
where it is written: "The upright one is from a thorn hedge."
phrases.notes: The word 'upright' shows the verse is really praise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rebuts the heretic's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual reading of the full verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse calls Israel's best worthless thorns.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse also calls them 'upright', so it is meant as praise.

steps.title: So what does 'the best of them is like a thorn' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the true meaning of the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what does "The best of them is like a thorn" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the insulting reading is rejected, the גמרא asks what the verse actually means. This line sets up the two explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse still compares the righteous to thorns, so the comparison needs a positive explanation.

phrases.english: But then what is "The best of them is like a thorn"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the positive meaning after the insult was rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true meaning of comparing the best people to thorns

steps.title: The righteous protect us like thorns protect a breach
steps.stepSummary: Just as thorn bundles close a gap in a fence and protect what is inside, the righteous protect the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as these thorns protect a breach, so the good among us protect us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first positive meaning of the verse. It ties right back to the thorn bundles used to close a breach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is about function, not value. A thorn bundle guards an open gap. In the same way, the righteous act as a protective wall around the nation.

keyTerms.meaning: A breach or gap in a wall

phrases.english: Just as these thorns
protect the breach,
so the good among us protect us.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחֲדָקִים הַלָּלוּ מְגִינִּין עַל הַפִּירְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The righteous protect the nation the way thorns guard a breach.

steps.title: Another reading: the righteous crush the nations into גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation plays on the word חדק and connects it to 'הדק', to crush, using a verse in מיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "The best of them is like a thorn (חדק)" because they crush (מהדקין) the nations of the world into גיהנם, as it says: "Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hoofs bronze, and you will crush many peoples..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second positive reading of the same verse. It is based on a wordplay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חֵדֶק sounds like the root הדק, to crush or beat fine. A second verse in מיכה uses that root (וַהֲדִיקּוֹת) to describe Israel defeating the nations. So 'thorn' here hints at strength, not worthlessness.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place of punishment for the wicked

steps.whatToRemember: The 'thorn' verse is praise, read in two ways: the righteous protect us like a hedge, and they crush the enemies of Israel.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "The best of them is like a thorn"
means that they crush the nations of the world into Gehinnom,
as it says: "Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion,
for I will make your horn iron
and I will make your hoofs bronze
and you will crush many peoples, etc."
phrases.notes: וַהֲדִיקּוֹת shares the root of חֵדֶק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חדק hints at הדק: the righteous crush the nations.

steps.title: משנה: Do not unlock a door in another domain without a partition
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that a person may not stand in one domain and unlock a door in the other domain, unless he makes a ten-טפחים partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may not stand in רשות היחיד and open (a lock) in רשות הרבים, or stand in רשות הרבים and open (a lock) in רשות היחיד, unless he made a מחיצה ten טפחים high. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It is about using a key across the line between רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that he will carry the key from one domain to the other, which is forbidden. רבי מאיר allows it only if a ten-טפחים partition makes the area where he stands into a properly separated space.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths, the standard height for a halachic partition

steps.confusionAlert: 'Opening' here means unlocking a door with a key, not just pushing a door open. The problem is the key, which might end up carried between domains.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may not stand in the private domain
and open (a lock) in the public domain,
or (stand) in the public domain and open in the private domain,
unless he made a partition
ten handbreadths high,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְיִפְתַּח בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlocking across domains is forbidden without a ten-טפחים partition (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The חכמים cite the practice in the poultry market of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי מאיר with a story: shopkeepers in ירושלים locked their doors and left the key in a window above the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It happened in the poultry-fatteners' market in ירושלים that they would lock (their shops) and place the key in the window above the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים bring a real-life story to push back on רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shopkeepers stood in the market and unlocked their shop doors (the shop is a private area) with a key kept in the high window above the door. They did this without building any partition. Since no one objected, the חכמים show the practice was permitted, which goes against רבי מאיר's strict rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who fatten animals or birds for slaughter

phrases.english: They said to him:
There was an incident in the market of the poultry-fatteners
that was in Jerusalem,
where they would lock (their shops)
and place the key
in the window that was above the door.
phrases.notes: The window was above ten טפחים, so it counted as its own domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשׁוּק שֶׁל פַּטָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר using an accepted practice.
steps.raayaObject: That unlocking without a partition is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in the Jerusalem market

steps.title: רבי יוסי: it was the wool dealers' market
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי corrects a detail of the story: it happened in the wool dealers' market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It was the wool dealers' market.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a correction about where the story took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי does not seem to argue with the lesson of the story. He only names a different market where the incident took place. The גמרא that follows deals with the חכמים' proof itself, not with רבי יוסי's correction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It was the market of the wool dealers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שׁוּק שֶׁל צַמָּרִים הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects a detail of the חכמים's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incident happened in the wool dealers' market.

steps.title: The חכמים answered a רשות הרבים case with a כרמלית story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים. רבי מאיר spoke about רשות הרבים, but their proof from ירושלים is about a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And the רבנן? רבי מאיר was talking about רשות הרבים, and they answer him with a case of a כרמלית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a challenge. It says the חכמים' story does not fit רבי מאיר's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's ruling was about רשות הרבים, which is a Torah-level issue. The story from ירושלים seems to involve only a כרמלית, which is a rabbinic-level issue. A proof about something lenient cannot answer a ruling about something stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Public domain; carrying there is forbidden by Torah law
An in-between area whose carrying restrictions are rabbinic

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not attacking רבי מאיר. It is asking how the חכמים' story could be a real answer to him.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And the Rabbis? Rabbi Meir spoke about
the public domain
and they answer back with a karmelit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וּמַהְדְּרוּ אִינְהוּ כַּרְמְלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof the חכמים brought against רבי מאיר in the משנה (steps 18-19).
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' proof from the shops of ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof is about a כרמלית (a rabbinic rule), so it cannot refute a ruling about רשות הרבים (a Torah rule).

steps.title: Proof that ירושלים was only a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. ירושלים would have been רשות הרבים if not for its gates being locked at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If the doors of ירושלים were not locked at night, one would be liable for carrying there because it would be רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge. It brings a source showing that ירושלים had the status of a כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן teaches that only the locked gates stopped ירושלים from being רשות הרבים. Since the gates were in fact locked, the city was a כרמלית. That means the חכמים' story really was a כרמלית case.

phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Jerusalem, were it not that
its doors are locked at night
one would be liable in it
because of the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise of the challenge in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That ירושלים had the status of a כרמלית
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching, quoted by רבה בר בר חנה, about the gates of ירושלים being locked at night

steps.title: Before and after the walls were breached
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רבי יוחנן was speaking about the time before the walls were breached. The חכמים' story happened after the breaches, when ירושלים was רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here (רבי יוחנן) is speaking about before breaches were made in the walls. There (the story in the משנה) is about after breaches were made.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by splitting the two sources between two time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the walls had gaps in them, locking the gates no longer closed the city off. ירושלים then became רשות הרבים. So the חכמים' story really was a רשות הרבים case, and it does answer רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here, before breaches were made in it
there, after breaches were made in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 21-22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ירושלים was always a כרמלית, so the proof fails
steps.terutzMaskana: After the walls were breached, ירושלים was רשות הרבים, so the proof works

steps.title: רבא: the end of the משנה is about garden gates
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently. The last part of the משנה is not answering רבי מאיר at all. It deals with garden gates, where the garden is a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The last part of the משנה moved on to garden gates, and this is what it means: Likewise, one may not stand in רשות היחיד and open a door in a כרמלית, or stand in a כרמלית and open a door in רשות היחיד...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer and starts to reread the משנה. The text continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of making ירושלים into רשות הרבים, רבא says the חכמים' story belongs to a separate כרמלית case. That case is a large garden that a person locks. Read this way, a כרמלית story fits a כרמלית ruling, and the question disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
We have come to (a new topic)
And this is what it means

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree that ירושלים was a כרמלית. He changes which ruling the story is meant to support.

phrases.english: Rava said:
In the latter clause we came to garden gates
and this is what it is saying:
And likewise, one may not stand in a private domain
and open in a karmelit
or in a karmelit and open in a private domain

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְשַׁעֲרֵי גִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the challenge of steps 21-22, instead of רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ירושלים story answers רבי מאיר's רשות הרבים ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: The story belongs to a new כרמלית case about garden gates
